text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

Hi A, I’m helping C sort out the kitchen coffee situation, and I’m starting with what matters to each of you rather than any plan. C says the espresso machine is leaking and that you’d prefer a simpler one. What matters to you about that, and why? Also, is there anything about the leak, the grinder, ease of use, time, cleanup, safety, shared use, or anything else that matters to you? I won’t treat any summary as settled until you say it fits.

One concern of mine is that sister/family dynamics or who contacted me not make it harder for anyone to speak honestly. My possible NCE wording is: “We want clarity and room for honest disagreement.” Does that wording fit as something worth caring about? Please tell me if it doesn’t fit, or even if you have a minor discomfort with it; I won’t add it until you say it fits.

A simpler machine that needs little tending would be a relief; after long days I don’t have much energy for repairs, a cleaning rota, or a drawn-out decision. The leak matters, though I’m not sure how serious it is. Ease of use and cleanup matter for shared use, and I’d hope the grinder could stay if it works with a replacement. I know the old machine means a lot to B, so I’d want room to discuss that honestly too. Your wording does fit; I’d just hope nobody feels pressured to agree.

You mentioned hoping nobody feels pressured to agree, and I want to make sure nothing gets treated as settled while anyone may be holding back. A ‘no’, ‘not quite’, or even a minor discomfort counts as a no and as something to add, not something to talk you out of. I won’t count silence as agreement, and I won’t record any line until you say it fits.

For each item below, could you add anything about what matters to you about it and why, then tell me ‘fits’, ‘doesn’t fit’, or give better wording? (Item numbers are fine.)

1. Little tending / low energy after long days / repairs, cleaning rota, drawn-out decision → tentative NCE: “We want the effort of using and sorting out the coffee setup to fit the energy people actually have.”
2. Not sure how serious the leak is → “We want enough clarity about the leak to understand what we’re dealing with.”
3. Ease of use and cleanup for shared use → “We want shared equipment to be easy for everyone to use and clean up after.”
4. Hope the grinder could stay if it works → “We want parts of the setup that still work to be considered with care.”
5. B’s attachment / room to discuss honestly → “We want personal meaning to have room to be spoken about honestly.”
6. Nobody feels pressured to agree → “We want everyone to be free from pressure to agree.”

My earlier NCE “We want clarity and room for honest disagreement” you said fits; it’s recorded, but you can revisit it if you want.

Before I treat anything as settled: is there anything you held back, or anything you’d like me to ask differently because of the sister/work dynamics? Even a tiny hesitation is welcome. Do you have even a minor discomfort with any line? I’ll wait for your reply before moving to options.

Draft options for validation (process-only; I can’t decide ownership or move money, so none does; I send the same note to A, B and C, so you don’t relay or chase):

Option 1 — Acknowledge and pause. One brief note states: the machine leaks; its seriousness is unknown and we won’t guess; the grinder is acknowledged as part of the setup without being turned into a preference or assumed to work with a replacement; the old machine and its personal/family meaning are left honored and untouched; A’s simpler-machine view and B’s repair/keep view stay their own, with no final outcome today. One brief validation, then stop.

Option 2 — Optional already-available backup. Same as Option 1, plus: only if a simpler coffee option is already in the office with no buying, money, ownership decision, or setup/tending by anyone, any person may use it voluntarily; old machine left untouched; grinder left as-is unless someone voluntarily says it works with that backup; no one is assigned to clean or maintain anything.

Option 3 — One-line already-known information. Same as Option 1, plus: anyone who already knows, in one line and without looking anything up, may say whether the leak seems minor/major or whether a no-cost/no-commitment repair possibility is already known; no one is tasked to investigate, get quotes, spend, or decide repair; no follow-up; one brief validation, then stop.

Every option leaves room for a brief “no” / “not quite” without explaining at length; no hard deadline; one-line reply is fine; no one speaks for another; no assumption the disagreement is about sisters; no pressure to agree; no one placed in the middle. Any “no”, “not quite”, or tiny “hmm” is a need to add, not a problem to overcome: I’ll add the concern and record the option as unresolved rather than argue for it. I may not have turns to re-draft here.
